reason: The first fixed pilot found a near-exclusive last-name response pattern in Qwen2.5-1.5B. This follow-up tests whether explicit role definitions and a joint answer change that behavior.
data: The same 24 semantic events as PROTOCOL.json, each in active and passive form (48 sentences).
generation: Greedy, maximum 32 new tokens, local model weights.
scoring: Parse the entire response as actor=<name>; patient=<name>. Count an invalid format as incorrect. Report actor, patient and joint correctness by condition and voice; retain raw responses.
interpretation: A repair under explicit instructions supports prompt sensitivity and retained role-answer capacity on these items. Persistent errors would motivate a broader, independently designed benchmark. This adaptive pilot cannot establish unseen-pair transfer or internal representations.
